title: You'll figure it out
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What did your parents tell you when you did not know what to do?
Jose asked: how was the concept of risk instilled in him? A student said: he sees his father's pursuit of entrepreneurial ideas and the risk he assumes.
Jose read a line from the book about the author's parents leaving the boys in a park.
it was insane to leave me and my brother alone in the park at that age.

Parents weren't overprotective like parents are today, Jose said. When you see parents with their children: be careful, don't do this, sit still, don't move. They are ingraining it. Other parents say: he's going to get dirty, who cares, go explore. That whole thing will influence your child forever, just the way you talk to them.

A student said: it was fascinating how many times they mention that he travelled alone on a train at ten. Along the way you learn that you dispose of time. Another said: every time you increase your risk appetite, it increases incrementally. Getting punched in the mouth is scary until you do, and then it's not so bad.

And what about the mom saying: you'll figure it out? Jose asked. That is a privilege. As parents we are contaminated by our own fear and instill it in our children: you've got to be a doctor, a lawyer, make money, study. We impose that view, at the danger of cutting off their idea of their future.

Schools can do that too, he said: they tell you everything you have to do. That's why some great entrepreneurs say: I figured out how to learn on my own. A student said they were homeschooled and taught themselves almost everything.

People will always tell you what you didn't study and what you don't know, Jose said. I always tell my children: you can do anything. You just have to understand how to absorb the information, be passionate, and develop habits where you don't get distracted. It is all about laser focus.
What do you tell yourself or others when they don't know what to do?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what your parents told you about risk.
Write one fear you were handed that was not yours.
Write what you can learn on your own.
Write a time you did something alone that scared you, and what it taught you.
Write the sentence you will say next time someone you lead says: I don't know how.

check.q: What did Jose call the mother's saying 'you'll figure it out'?
What did Jose say we do as parents out of our own fear?
choices: Instill it in our children and impose our view of their future

check.q: What did Jose say it is all about?

recap: Tell people they'll figure it out. Don't hand them your fear.
